subject: Operational commitments for uplift and co-terming
messages:
From: Liz Wu <liz.wu@omniretail.com>
To: irene_choi@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@omniretail.com
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal — uplift / co-term questions

Hi Irene,

Quick context: OmniRetail is planning a Q4 rollout expansion across 3 product lines and we expect a 2.5–3x token increase. Procurement asked me to confirm options for: staged discounts as usage grows, co-terming to align renewal on 12/31, and any SLA carve-outs if we add burst capacity mid-contract.

Can you send a proposed structure we can share with finance and ops? Also include what would trigger price breakpoints and whether additional capacity requires legal signoff or can be handled by an amendment.

Thanks — Liz

Liz Wu
Head of Integrations, OmniRetail
From: irene_choi@redwood.com
To: Liz Wu <liz.wu@omniretail.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, jordan_blake@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal — uplift / co-term questions

Liz — thanks for the detail and congrats on the expansion. High level we can do a staged uplift with 3 buckets (baseline / growth / surge) and an annual co-term to 12/31. Key points in the attached workbook: pricing ladder, breakpoint definitions (tokens per month over 30/90/180 day rolling averages), and an "operational commitment" column that maps SLA impacts to pricing.

Quick answers:
- Discounts: incremental discount tiers at 20%/35%/50% vs baseline per-token rate as you cross breakpoints. We can structure as automatic triggers (ops signals) with a reconciliation invoice, or as pre-purchased uplift buckets.
- Co-terming: we support mid-contract co-term via an amendment; pro-rata applied to remaining months. No need for a full SOW if both parties sign the amendment (standard flow).
- SLA carve-outs for burst: we can offer a best-effort burst lane with reserved priority capacity; if you need guaranteed latency during bursts we need a dedicated pool (contract + capacity commitment). That does require legal review for SLA language but operations can provision once paperwork is signed.

I put Ben on copy for pricing mechanics and Jordan for the rollout timeline / ops handoff. I'll follow up with a one-page summary for procurement.

— Irene
Irene Choi
Enterprise Lead, Redwood Inference
From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: Liz Wu <liz.wu@omniretail.com>
Cc: irene_choi@redwood.com, jordan_blake@redwood.com, procurement@omniretail.com
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 12:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal — uplift / co-term questions

Liz — attaching a workbook with two commercial paths: 1) staged committed buckets with stepped discounts and credit carryforward rules, and 2) automatic trigger model with monthly reconciliation (simpler operationally but higher unit price during surge). See sheet "Summary" for tradeoffs.

Operational notes:
- Breakpoints are evaluated on a 90-day rolling baseline to avoid noisy spikes.
- If you choose reserved surge (dedicated pool), minimum 6-month commitment on that pool to protect scheduling on GPUs.
- Legal: amendments cover co-term and bucket adds; larger capacity adds that exceed 2x baseline will likely require a pricing review.

Next step: which approach does procurement prefer? If they want minimal legal work, path #1 (pre-purchased buckets) shortens turnaround.

Attachment: redwood_uplift_pricing_v2.xlsx (pricing ladder + examples)

— Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: procurement@omniretail.com
To: ben_carter@redwood.com, irene_choi@redwood.com
Cc: Liz Wu <liz.wu@omniretail.com>
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 09:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal — uplift / co-term questions

Hi Ben / Irene,

Procurement reviewed both paths. A few clarifying asks before we move to legal:
1) For pre-purchased buckets, can unused capacity be applied as credits toward the next quarter (we prefer carryforward up to 90 days)?
2) For the dedicated pool SLA, what is the expected provisioning lead time and what credit formula would apply if the pool underperforms latency targets?
3) Can you provide a sample amendment template that only includes co-term and bucket mechanics (so our legal can redline quickly)?

Can you also confirm whether the 20%/35%/50% discounts are stackable with any enterprise volume rebates we have on the renewal?

Thanks,
OmniRetail Procurement
From: jordan_blake@redwood.com
To: procurement@omniretail.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: irene_choi@redwood.com, Liz Wu <liz.wu@omniretail.com>
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal — uplift / co-term questions

All — quick answers inline:
1) Carryforward: yes, unused pre-purchased tokens can carry forward up to 90 days and apply to the next invoice (we'll add rules for pro-rata consumption).
2) Provisioning lead time: 10 business days for standard reserved pool spin-up; urgent provisioning has a 3–5 business day option at a startup fee. Credit formula: service credits tied to percent of SLA breach (standard credit matrix in appendix B of the SLA). We'll send the exact numbers in the amendment template.
3) Amendment template: attaching a clean copy that only covers co-term mechanics, bucket definitions, and SLA carveouts — this should minimize legal back-and-forth.

Regarding stacking: discounts in the uplift ladder are applied before any account-level volume rebate; finance can model the net effective rate. If you want us to bake in an example scenario for your finance team we can do a short model.

Attaching: OMNIRETAIL_MA_plan.docx (amendment draft)

— Jordan
Jordan Blake
Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference
